units.function: CLI tests for Plugin project scaffolding, local-versus-registry install request resolution and target-server health diagnostics.
units.dependencyDirection: The Vitest suite mocks the first-party create-paperclip-plugin scaffolder, registers the Plugin Commander module, creates temporary local directories and injects a health GET function; it tests option mapping and diagnostic formatting without installing or executing a Plugin.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin package name, output directory, template/category/display metadata, SDK path, registry version/local-path flag and target health fields including version, deploymentMode and deploymentExposure.
units.lifecycle: Map CLI flags into scaffold options; print next development/install commands; resolve an existing path as a local Plugin or retain an npm package/version; probe /api/health and report reachable target identity/mode or remediation text.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 10/10 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. It covers scoped package naming, paths with spaces, wrapper delegation, local/registry resolution and health success/failure formatting. It omits invalid names/paths, existing-output collision, package integrity/signature, dependency install, Plugin manifest/capability validation, compatibility, sandboxing and actual target install behavior.
units.designRationale: Offer a low-friction official Plugin development path while reducing accidental installation to the wrong local/remote server by showing target health, version and deployment mode.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a governed Connector/Plugin developer experience that works across managed-cloud and self-hosted targets, makes the destination and compatibility explicit, and prevents third-party code from escaping capability, secret, data and responsibility boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the target-diagnostics and thin official-scaffolder delegation patterns. Company OS should own its Connector SDK/schema, distinguish declarative Connector packages from executable Plugins, pin integrity/provenance, validate capabilities and compatibility, and require explicit trust/install policy. Do not copy Paperclip branding, package names, generated templates or internal SDK paths.
units.responsibilityConflict: Scaffolding metadata and target reachability do not establish who may install executable code, what data/tools it can access, which accountable human accepts its risk or how its actions enter the responsibility chain.

securityFindings: Local-path detection and registry fallback are tested, but symlinks, ownership, world-writable paths, path canonicalization and ambiguous missing relative paths are not.
Registry installs have no tested lockfile, exact-version requirement, checksum/signature, publisher provenance, allowlist or dependency-vulnerability gate.
Generated next commands interpolate a single-quoted path; apostrophes, newlines and shell metacharacters are untested, so displayed copy/paste commands require robust shell escaping.
Health diagnostics trust and display server-provided version/mode and raw reachability errors without testing transport security, server identity, certificate validation or secret redaction.
Scaffolder tests do not cover overwrite refusal, template path traversal, generated dependency pinning, license notices or executable postinstall scripts.
No Plugin capability, secret, network/filesystem, data-export or tenant-isolation policy is exercised before installation.
